Title: API returns HTTP 403 with empty body instead of the real error status (400/401/404/405/409/415/500)
Environment: Commit fc1f1cc; Windows 11; JDK 17.0.12; Node 22.21; MySQL 8.0.45 (tastelanka_qa); Edge 154; see test-environment.md
Description: Every error produced by a controller (validation, not found, conflict, bad credentials, method not allowed, unsupported media type and unhandled 500s) reaches the client as 403 Forbidden with Content-Length 0. Holds for anonymous and authenticated (including ADMIN) requests. Clients cannot show validation feedback or distinguish errors; server errors are hidden.
Steps to Reproduce: 1) POST /api/v1/auth/register with body {}  2) POST /api/v1/auth/login with a wrong password  3) GET /api/v1/restaurants/does-not-exist  4) As ADMIN, POST /api/v1/admin/restaurants with slug 'nuga-gama'
Expected Result: 400 / 401 / 404 / 409 with an error body describing the problem
Actual Result: 403 with empty body in every case (backend log shows the correct exception was resolved, e.g. MethodArgumentNotValidException, then masked)
Root Cause (if known): Servlet error dispatch to /error is not permitted in SecurityConfig and the stateless JWT context is not present on the ERROR dispatch, so Spring Security denies /error (403). MockMvc (no error dispatch) returns the correct statuses – confirmed by ApiIntegrationTest TC-INT-002/003/004 passing while HttpErrorContractTest fails.
Retest Result: Not retested – no fix delivered in this cycle

Title: Default JWT signing secret committed in application.yml allows forging admin tokens
Environment: Commit fc1f1cc; Windows 11; JDK 17.0.12; Node 22.21; MySQL 8.0.45 (tastelanka_qa); Edge 154; see test-environment.md
Description: application.yml falls back to a hard-coded JWT secret when JWT_SECRET is not set. The README run steps never set JWT_SECRET for the API (only .env for Docker MySQL), so a default start-up uses the public secret. A token forged offline with this secret for the admin e-mail is accepted, giving full administrator access without credentials.
Preconditions: API started per README (JWT_SECRET unset). Attacker knows/guesses an admin e-mail.
Steps to Reproduce: 1) Build HS256 JWT {sub: admin email, exp: +1h} signed with the secret from application.yml  2) GET /api/v1/admin/dashboard with it
Expected Result: 401/403 – token not issued by the server is rejected; application refuses to start with a default secret
Root Cause (if known): Insecure default `${JWT_SECRET:change-this-development-secret-...}` in application.yml; no start-up guard.
Retest Result: Not retested – no fix delivered in this cycle
